eventClusters.statement: Thermal-coal input prices fell sharply in Q2 while official industrial-profit data showed electricity/heat/gas/water profits rising strongly against broad industrial weakness, creating a direct cost-spread opportunity for power generators.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Falling coal hurts miners but can expand generator margins. Deep research must verify company fuel-cost sensitivity and realized profit conversion rather than assume all utilities benefit equally.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Which A-share thermal-power generator had already realized coal-cost margin recovery and retained valuation/asymmetry room?

eventClusters.statement: China domestic aviation demand returned to or above pre-pandemic holiday levels during Q2 and monthly passenger traffic recovered sharply, but load factors and international capacity were not fully normalized.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Traffic recovery does not guarantee airline profit because fuel, yields, capacity and international mix matter. Deep research must require realized unit-economics improvement.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Did any A-share airline/airport convert passenger recovery into a measurable earnings bridge before June-end?

eventClusters.statement: Lithium carbonate reversed upward after a five-month collapse as EV/storage demand and restocking recovered, but supply growth was expected to cap the rebound, creating a potentially short-lived turning-point rather than a clean structural upcycle.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: A higher lithium price helps upstream but pressures cells/EVs; the rebound may be capped by supply. Turning-point candidates require explicit operating leverage and survival/working-capital checks.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Is there a listed lithium producer with a real price-to-profit turning-point bridge, or is the rebound too supply-capped/anticipated?

eventClusters.statement: NDRC reset regional/provincial transmission tariffs under the third regulatory cycle from June 1, but the immediate listed-company earnings incidence was not clear from the policy text alone.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Policy is real but earnings incidence depends on regulated asset bases and cost allocation; no direct company engine is visible at discovery.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Keep as policy context unless company-level regulated-return impact can be quantified.

eventClusters.statement: China manufacturing PMI remained below 50 through May-June while broad industrial profits were still falling, even as selected reopening/cost-spread sectors improved.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Useful as macro context and a timing challenge, not a narrow long opportunity.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Use as a contradiction filter for company engines rather than promote a standalone stock thesis.
